topics.topic_title: Self-Balancing Binary Search Trees (AVL & Red-Black Trees)

questions.question: Which fundamental physical/mathematical principle directly underpins Self-Balancing Binary Search Trees (AVL & Red-Black Trees)?

options.text: Conservation of energy and continuous state differentiability
Unbounded positive exponential divergence in open loop
Strict static linearity without dynamical evolution
Zero-order hold with infinite sampling latency

questions.explanation: In Self-Balancing Binary Search Trees (AVL & Red-Black Trees), governing equations are derived from physical conservation laws and boundary continuity.

distractor_analysis.B: Unbounded divergence indicates instability, not the governing principle.
distractor_analysis.C: Most real systems exhibit dynamical time-evolution.
distractor_analysis.D: Zero-order hold is a sampling artifact, not a foundational law.

questions.question: For a system configured as in Self-Balancing Binary Search Trees (AVL & Red-Black Trees), given operating parameter alpha = 2.0 and input step u(t) = 5.0, calculate the steady-state equilibrium value.
steps: Step 1: Set time derivatives to zero in steady state: dx/dt = 0

questions.question: In a safety-critical deployment of Self-Balancing Binary Search Trees (AVL & Red-Black Trees), if feedback noise variance increases by 10 dB, what compensator adjustment is necessary to prevent actuator saturation while preserving stability?

options.text: Increase high-frequency loop gain to track noise
Introduce high-frequency roll-off (low-pass filtering) in the feedback path
Eliminate the integral term and reduce phase margin to 0 degrees
Double the sampling rate without anti-aliasing filtering

questions.explanation: Adding high-frequency roll-off attenuates noise amplification outside the control bandwidth, preventing actuator saturation.

distractor_analysis.A: Increasing high-frequency gain amplifies noise and causes saturation.
distractor_analysis.C: Zero phase margin results in marginal instability and oscillation.
distractor_analysis.D: Doubling sampling without anti-aliasing causes aliasing foldover.
